newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Arafat urges Europe to help further peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Arafat urges Europe to help further peace talks.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held talks with Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima on Tuesday and repeated his plea for European intervention to breathe life into the Middle East peace process.

"We are facing some troubles and I am looking to (Viktor Klima), to Europe, to the international community to protect the peace process. We are in need of help," Arafat told reporters after a 90-minute meeting with Klima.
"The European Union should more and more push its role in the peace process. We have reached a stalemate."
Formal negotiations between the Palestinians and Israel have been frozen since March when Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Arafat's stopover in Vienna followed a two-day visit to London, where he met British Prime Minister Tony Blair. Britain and Austria will both hold the European Union's six-month rotating presidency next year.
Earlier, in a speech in London to academics and politicians, Arafat called on Europe to use economic sanctions to prevent Israel building new settlements in occupied territories.

"Seventy percent of the economy of Israel is with European countries and this card has not been used until now..You only have to wave this economic card and they will listen to you directly," Arafat said.
Klima assured Arafat that Austria would do its utmost to move the Middle East peace process forward.
He also promised his country's backing for a Palestinian resolution urging the United Nations to take action against Israel for refusing to halt construction of settlements.
"As you know, Austria has condemned the Israeli acts and, as you know, Austria supports the Palestinians' General Assembly resolution," Klima said.
Arafat underlined his own commitment to peace with Israel, saying: "We cannot see another alternative but to continue with the peace process in spite of all the troubles we are facing."
He put the cost to the Palestinians of Israeli border closures alone at seven million to nine million dollars a day.

Israel has periodically sealed off the West Bank and Gaza for security reasons since part of the territories came under self-rule in 1994. More than 60,000 Palestinians held jobs in Israel before 1994.
Klima promised that the Austrian government would continue to offer economic aid to the Palestinians, targeted at education, health care and infrastructure projects.
Arafat was due to leave Austria on Wednesday afternoon after a lunch-time meeting with parliamentary president Heinz Fischer.
